The Trump-Netanyahu Partnership: The Middle East Gains That Must Not Be Squandered gatestoneinstitute.org/22915… The Trump-Netanyahu Partnership: The Middle East Gains That Must Not Be Squandered by Bassam Tawil October 12, 2026 at 5:00 am  The Middle East... remains far from stable. Hamas continues to resist disarmament, Iran remains a major threat, and Hezbollah's armed presence in Lebanon continues to undermine the authority of the Lebanese state. The future of Gaza, including who will govern it and who will control its weapons, stands unresolved.  Can Gaza really have a new beginning while the organization that launched the October 7, 2023 massacre retains the ability to obstruct the transition and launch more massacres -- not just of Israelis but of its own citizens and other neighbors?  The achievements of recent months could be weakened, or even reversed, if the remaining challenges are left unresolved.  The question is no longer simply what Washington and Jerusalem have achieved together. It is whether they can turn those achievements into lasting security.  A ceasefire without disarmament, a transitional administration without operational authority, and military victories without a strategy for the future will leave the region exposed to endless instability.  The task ahead is therefore clear: turn the gains already made into a strategic reality in which Palestinians in Gaza can live under civilian government rather than an armed factional rule; in which Israel's security is strengthened, and in which Iran and its Middle Eastern allies can no longer threaten its own people or the region in any way.  The question is no longer simply what Washington and Jerusalem have achieved together. It is whether they can turn those achievements into lasting security. Pictured: U.S. President Donald Trump shakes hands with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a press conference on December 29, 2025 in Palm Beach, Florida. (Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images) Over the past year and a half, the Middle East has undergone dramatic changes. Israel, increasingly encircled for decades by an Iranian "noose of fire" on seven fronts, inflicted severe damage on its enemies' military capabilities; the United States finally demonstrated its willingness to use military force against the Islamic Republic of Iran, and a US-backed agreement brought home all the Israeli hostages still held by Hamas.  President Donald J. Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu played central roles in these developments. Their partnership combined America's diplomatic leverage and military power with Israel's intelligence capabilities and military operations.  The Middle East, nevertheless, remains far from stable. Hamas continues to resist disarmament, Iran remains a major threat, and Hezbollah's armed presence in Lebanon continues to undermine the authority of the Lebanese state. The future of Gaza, including who will govern it and who will control its weapons, stands unresolved.  The question is no longer simply what Washington and Jerusalem have achieved together. It is whether they can turn those achievements into lasting security.  One of the most consequential developments was the US-backed Gaza ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025. The agreement ended the period of large-scale fighting and led to the return of all the remaining living Israeli hostages held by Hamas.  For the families who endured months of uncertainty and suffering, the return of their loved ones was an enormous achievement. It also demonstrated the potential of American diplomatic pressure, regional mediation, and Israeli military pressure to produce results that years of negotiations had failed to secure.  Trump's 20-point plan subsequently provided a framework for a different future for Gaza. It envisioned an end to Hamas's rule, the disarmament of armed factions, a transitional Palestinian administration, an International Stabilization Force (ISF), and reconstruction.  In January 2026, the Board of Peace was formally launched, with Trump as its chairman. Its mandate was to help oversee the transition and create the conditions for Gaza to be governed without the political or military domination of the terrorist group Hamas.  There has been progress in building the institutional framework. The National Committee for the Administration of Gaza has been established, preparations have been made to recruit and train Palestinian police, and the international community has developed a roadmap for disarmament.  The most difficult tasks, however, remain unfinished.  A report submitted by the Board of Peace to the UN Security Council in May acknowledged that negotiations over the implementation roadmap had not been finalized. The proposed ISF was still preparing for deployment, while the disarmament of Hamas and other armed terrorist factions remains a central obstacle.  Hamas has suffered substantial military loses, but as a political and armed force, it has not disappeared. Its continued presence raises a fundamental question: Can Gaza really have a new beginning while the organization that launched the October 7, 2023 massacre retains the ability to obstruct the transition and launch more massacres -- not just of Israelis but of its own citizens and other neighbors?  The answer will determine whether the ceasefire becomes the foundation of a lasting settlement or merely an interval before another round of fighting.  The other historic development was the military confrontation with Iran in June 2025.  Israel, on June 13, 2025, launched Operation Rising Lion, striking Iranian nuclear infrastructure, missile production facilities, air defenses, military headquarters, and senior military commanders. On June 22, the United States struck three Iranian nuclear facilities at Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan.  The operations demonstrated a level of US-Israeli military coordination with massive implications for regional security. They inflicted damage on important elements of Iran's military and nuclear infrastructure and demonstrated that Iran's geographical distance and extensive defensive preparations could not guarantee the protection of its most sensitive facilities.  The main challenge is still to prevent Iran from restoring the capabilities that made it such a serious threat to Israel and other countries in the region. This objective requires sustained intelligence cooperation, effective monitoring, credible deterrence, and a clear response to attempts to rebuild prohibited or threatening capabilities.  The challenge extends beyond Gaza and Iran.  Hezbollah's decision to build an extensive military infrastructure outside the authority of the Lebanese state has contributed to decades of instability along Israel's northern border. Hezbollah's relationship with Iran was what gave the country the means of projecting military power beyond its own territory.  Efforts to strengthen the Lebanese state's authority and dismantle Hezbollah's independent military capabilities -- as well as those of Iran's other terrorist proxies, Hamas and the Houthis -- remain essential to any durable regional settlement.  A Lebanon in which the rightful government exercises unobstructed control over the country's armed forces and territory would be in the interests of both Lebanese citizens and their neighbors.  The same principle applies to Gaza. Civilian institutions cannot function effectively when an armed faction retains the power to threaten and overrule them.  The Trump-Netanyahu partnership has also operated against the background of the Abraham Accords, which established diplomatic relations between Israel and several Arab states during Trump's first administration. These agreements remain an important foundation for the possibility of broader regional cooperation.  Trump and Netanyahu have helped bring about long-sought-after changes in the regional balance of power. Military success and diplomatic breakthroughs, however, are not ends in themselves. Their significance ultimately depends on what follows.  The opportunity is significant, but it is not guaranteed. The achievements of recent months could be weakened, or even reversed, if the remaining challenges are left unresolved.  A ceasefire without disarmament, a transitional administration without operational authority, and military victories without a strategy for the future will leave the region exposed to endless instability.  The task ahead is therefore clear: turn the gains already made into a strategic reality in which Palestinians in Gaza can live under civilian government rather than an armed factional rule; in which Israel's security is strengthened, and in which Iran and its Middle Eastern allies can no longer threaten its own people or the region in any way.  Bassam Tawil is a Muslim Arab based in the Middle East. His work is made possible through the generous donation of a couple who wish to remain anonymous. Gatestone is most grateful.

🚨🇫🇷 GlassWorm-linked actors hijacked OVHcloud CLI releases to spread credential-stealing malware  A compromised developer GitHub account was used to replace binaries attached to OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 on October 19. ⠀ The malicious downloads were available between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC and were downloaded approximately 250 times. Only users who installed or updated the CLI during that window are affected. Earlier downloads of those versions remain safe. ⠀ The malware targeted data belonging to VS Code, Cursor, Claude, OpenCode and other developer tools, alongside AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, npm, DigitalOcean, SSH and Terraform credentials. ⠀ OVHcloud traced the compromise to GitHub credentials stolen after a developer installed a malicious VS Code extension on a personal MacBook in October 2025. Infrastructure linked to the incident contained indicators previously associated with GlassWorm. ⠀ OVHcloud says its source code and build systems were not compromised and no other repositories were affected. The malicious files were removed, release immutability was enabled and version 0.16.0 was published as a clean release.  Anyone who ran an affected binary should treat secrets stored on that system as compromised, revoke or rotate them, remove the binary and install version 0.16.0.

🚨 EXPOSED SERVERS REVEAL AN AI-ASSISTED RANSOMWARE WORKBENCH TIED TO INC AND THE GENTLEMEN  A threat research report published Oct 20, 2026 describes seven exposed adversary servers used by affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware operations, with 62 targeted organizations and more than $23,920 spent on commercial AI services. The investigation began in late September, after operator OPSEC failures left the servers' open directories exposed.  What the report says the servers held: • OpenCode AI session logs (8,257 messages across 133 sessions) using commercial models: the AI planned recon, generated commands and triaged stolen data, but waited for the human operator's approval before every step • Source code for "Phantom", an autonomous red-team framework with 18 skill modules, alongside Ghost C2, RevSocks, MCP servers and exfiltration tools; plus extortion procedures and scripted vishing • 46 custom INC encryptor builds for six victims, packed on Sep 30 for a planned Oct 1 deployment wave • A Sep 30 screenshot showing the encryptor running on one victim workstation • Operator records of mass exploitation of FortiClient EMS (CVE-2026-35616), SimpleHelp (CVE-2024-57727) and cPanel/WHM (CVE-2026-41940); those counts are the operators' own and not independently verified  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is firsthand research from the team that found the servers, not independent validation. The researchers link the workbench to both INC and The Gentlemen operations but rate a formal alliance as low confidence; a shared tooling environment used by several partners is the more likely model. Staged builds do not prove deployment: the planned Oct 1 encryption wave is unconfirmed beyond the one workstation screenshot. The report grades organizations by depth of activity, including reconnaissance-only targets; DDW does not name them, and none should be read as a confirmed breach. Defenders: patch FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp and cPanel/WHM, check EMS for unauthorized admin accounts, and lock down RMM tools.  Source: socradar.io/resources/whitep… #DDW #DarkWeb #Ransomware #AISecurity #INCRansomware #TheGentlemen #ThreatIntelligence

sample_tweets.text: Since my posts have been shared here ~30 times in the past few weeks, it seems like I'm going to be contributing to Space Karen's Ketamine Extravaganza whether I like it or not.  I don't really intend to be active here, but I'll post some of the more important cybersecurity-focused stuff, since it gets screenshotted anyway. That way, people don't have to read post a week late and out of context.

Current information I have on php2Shell:  - The RCEs requires the attacker to obtain memory addresses which are typically protected by ASLR.  - I suspect the original author (lcfr_hax) likely has a reliable exploit which leads to stable code execution.  - Most of the PoCs being posted are completely non-functional AI slop.  - There is at least 1 working non-slop exploit being passed around, but it's reliant on bruteforcing for ASLR bypass, so not particularly impactful.  - Rumor of ITW exploitation are patchy. There are attempts being seen using the non-functional leaked RCE, or variants that are config / system specific.  - Some rumors point towards a known-working exploit being used by threat actors (I've personally confirmed this specific exploit works, but the ASLR bypass technique is unreliable at best and massively limits the potential impact).  - I'd expect heavy ITW exploitation in the next few weeks based on how many people are looking at this. Though, success rates will vary heavily based on the specific exploit chain.

🚨🇫🇷 GlassWorm-linked actors hijacked OVHcloud CLI releases to spread credential-stealing malware A compromised developer GitHub account was used to replace binaries attached to OVHcloud CLI releases v0.11.0 through v0.15.0 on October 19. ⠀ The malicious downloads were available between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC and were downloaded approximately 250 times. Only users who installed or updated the CLI during that window are affected. Earlier downloads of those versions remain safe. ⠀ The malware targeted data belonging to VS Code, Cursor, Claude, OpenCode and other developer tools, alongside AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Docker, Kubernetes, npm, DigitalOcean, SSH and Terraform credentials. ⠀ OVHcloud traced the compromise to GitHub credentials stolen after a developer installed a malicious VS Code extension on a personal MacBook in October 2025. Infrastructure linked to the incident contained indicators previously associated with GlassWorm. ⠀ OVHcloud says its source code and build systems were not compromised and no other repositories were affected. The malicious files were removed, release immutability was enabled and version 0.16.0 was published as a clean release. Anyone who ran an affected binary should treat secrets stored on that system as compromised, revoke or rotate them, remove the binary and install version 0.16.0.

🚨 LiteLLM 1.107.0 compromised to steal cloud, developer and AI credentials LiteLLM, an open-source gateway used to connect applications with multiple AI providers, was compromised through a malicious release published on PyPI and official container registries. ⠀ All seven LiteLLM 1.107.0 wheels were affected across Windows, macOS and Linux. The malware uses Python startup files to execute whenever Python launches, even if LiteLLM is never imported. ⠀ Researchers found it targeting: • AWS, Azure and Google Cloud credentials • Kubernetes, Vault and Terraform secrets • SSH, GPG and TLS private keys • Git tokens, .env files and browser data • Credentials for Codex, Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf and Hugging Face ⠀ A separate loader was designed to check attacker-controlled infrastructure every hour and execute additional Python code. PyPI and Docker Hub have removed the malicious release and affected images. Anyone who installed LiteLLM 1.107.0 or pulled the latest, main-latest or main-stable container tags while they pointed to it should isolate affected systems, rotate accessible credentials from a clean device and rebuild from a trusted release.

🚨🇮🇳 State Bank of India investigates dark web exposure of customer records State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender, says it identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information while examining approximately 375,000 records found on the dark web. ⠀ The exposed information reportedly includes names, gender, mobile numbers, dates of birth, email and residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs and metadata linked to loan records. ⠀ SBI was alerted on October 16 by its threat intelligence provider, India’s Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. The bank activated its incident response procedures and hired an independent cybersecurity firm to investigate the source and extent of the exposure. ⠀ SBI says its core operations remain unaffected and customer balances are safe. The authenticity and completeness of the exposed data are still being assessed. Source: https://www. ndtv.com/business-news/sbi-dat a-leak-cyberattack-customer-account-phone-records-hacker-dark-web-12213824
